source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Frame, p.2-1

procedures.title: Frame: general description
notes: The Corvette frame is a stiff perimeter frame with five crossmembers.
Ahead of the rear kick-up, closed trapezoid-section side members surround and guard the passenger compartment.
At the cowl the side members sweep inward in an "S" curve, giving a base for the engine mounts and room for front wheel travel.
Behind the kick-up, box-section side rails carry the rear axle and suspension.
All five crossmembers are welded in, including the front one, which used to be bolted.

procedures.title: Frame alignment: check
steps: Check frame alignment (along with steering geometry and wheel alignment) on any car in an accident that could have bent the frame.
Set the car on a level surface with its weight on the wheels.
Look the frame over first; obvious damage often shows without measuring.
Step 1: X-check horizontally with a tram between matching points on opposite sides, tram points centered on each locating point and cross bar level.
If the two diagonals of any section differ by more than 3/16", the frame needs correction.
Without a tram gauge, hang a plumb bob from each reference point on a level floor, mark the floor under its tip, and measure between the marks with a rule.
Step 2: check the vertical dimensions from the datum plane to each point being trammed.
After repair, set the tram to the specified dimension and recheck.
notes: With correct settings the tram bar lies parallel to the frame, unless a reference point is itself in the damaged area.
Hole dimensions are taken to the dead center of the hole, flush with the surrounding metal.
